subject: Escalation: Gate and hot-swap request for Palmera dedicated pool
messages:
From: Julia Kline <julia@palmera.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@palmera.io
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: unexpected GPU preemption affecting Palmera private pool

Hi Soojin,

We're seeing widespread preemptions out of our dedicated pool in us-west-2 starting ~08:50 PDT. Jobs that normally run on the pinned pool are being moved or killed, which is causing inference errors for production customers. We've attached a short log extract and a spreadsheet where we recorded failed job IDs.

This is impacting Palmera's revenue-critical tenants — some SLAs are at risk. Can Redwood triage and (a) confirm whether this is a policy-driven reclaim, capacity contention with other deals, or a runtime fault, and (b) provide a temporary allocation or hot-swap so we can keep critical jobs running while you investigate?

We have a signed Dedicated contract (PALM-2026-09) with a 99.9% availability commitment; legal/ops are looped here. If you need additional context I can get an on-call engineer on the line.

Thanks,
Julia Kline
Head of Platform Operations
Palmera Inc

Attachments: palmera_preemption_log_20260914.csv, palmera_job_failures_0908-0915.xlsx
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Julia Kline <julia@palmera.io>, ops@palmera.io
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Urgent: unexpected GPU preemption affecting Palmera private pool

Folks — Julia's reported preemptions in Palmera's dedicated pool (PALM-2026-09). Initial notes: failures started ~08:50 PDT across a mix of model sizes; Palmera believes these are preemptions rather than OOMs. Julia attached logs + a job failure matrix.

Immediate asks:
- Marcus: can you run the capacity-impact calc (20 / 40 / 60% burst scenarios) and confirm which pools can spare capacity without violating other reserved commitments? Attach to this thread.
- Tessa: check contract language for emergency remediation commitments and whether a short-term quota transfer requires legal sign-off.
- Karthik: if we approve a hot-swap, what's the fastest runway to shuttle workloads (time to reassign, warm KV caches, expected latency delta)?

I'll flag this to the Allocation Board if we see cross-deal contention. For now, mark Palmera as urgent P1. Julia — we'll aim to respond with a proposed mitigation in ~90 minutes.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Dir, Customer Reliability 
Redwood Inference
Ops: +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Julia Kline <julia@palmera.io>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Urgent: unexpected GPU preemption affecting Palmera private pool

On Tue, Sep 14, 2026 at 09:12 AM Julia Kline <julia@palmera.io> wrote:
> We're seeing widespread preemptions out of our dedicated pool ...

Quick run of the numbers (summary):
- Palmera pool size: 48 A100-style vGPUs dedicated.
- Observed reclaim rate: ~18% of instances got preempted in short window.
- Current free headroom in non-critical reserved pools: ~12 vGPUs (can be rebalanced in ~30–45 min with minimal customer impact).
- Recommended temporary mitigation: grant Palmera a 20% burst (9 vGPU-equivalents) from low-priority reserve for a maximum 24-hour window while we investigate root cause.

Proposed gating & hot-swap mechanics:
1) Gate: create a short-lived allocation hold (palmera-burst-20260914) that pins 9 vGPU-equivalents to Palmera with higher preemption penalty on non-critical workloads. This prevents further eviction of Palmera jobs.
2) Hot-swap: if a pinned instance fails, automatically re-route traffic to warm spare instances in the same AZ; prioritize warm caches for top-10 endpoints (we maintain warm snapshots). Estimated latency delta: +40–120ms p95 for affected endpoints.
3) Quota rollback guardrails: schedule an automated rollback at 24 hours unless extended by Allocation Board approval; log all reroutes for audit.

Attachments: capacity_impact_estimate_v1.pdf (detailed calc), hot_swap_runbook_draft.md

Callouts: if this is policy-driven reclaim due to higher-priority Dedicated commitments, we'll need to evaluate whether commitments were overbooked. Tessa — that ties to contract remediation and any SLA credit exposure.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Product Ops Manager, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Julia Kline <julia@palmera.io>, ops@palmera.io
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Escalation: Gate and hot-swap request for Palmera dedicated pool

Julia — thank you for your patience and for the logs. We stood up the emergency gating described below at 16:00 PDT today. Summary of actions taken and next steps: 

What we did:
- Provisioned palmera-burst-20260914: +9 vGPU-equivalent burst from non-critical reserves in us-west-2 (hot-swap enabled).
- Enabled automatic reroute to warm instances for Palmera's top-10 endpoints. Expected p95 latency impact: +~80ms for rerouted traffic.
- Enabled audit logging for all preemptions and reroutes; we've attached the initial post-mortem stub.

What we will do next:
- Allocation Board review at 09:00 PDT tomorrow (2026-09-17) to determine whether we should extend the burst beyond 24 hours or reassign capacity more permanently.
- Marcus will publish the capacity-impact PDF and a recommended rollback plan.
- Tessa/Legal to advise on SLA language and whether a formal remediation credit applies; we'll coordinate external comms after that determination.

If Palmera agrees to proceed with the hot-swap window and confirms acceptance of the latency delta, we'll keep the temporary allocation in effect. Julia — please reply here with a short confirmation and whether you'd like an immediate incident bridge.

Sincerely,
Soojin Lee
Dir, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_impact_estimate_v1.pdf, hot_swap_runbook_draft.md, palmera_postmortem_stub.md
